title: Prematurity insults remodel cerebellar development and behaviour
title_zh: 早产损伤重塑小脑发育与行为
abstract: Abstract Preterm survivors often develop motor and socio-cognitive impairments that implicate altered cerebellar development, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. A key challenge is that prematurity involves overlapping perinatal insults that converge on the developing brain, making their individual effects difficult to disentangle. Here, we model two major prematurity-associated insults, maternal immune activation (MIA) and neonatal hypoxia (Hx), in mice. By controlling timing and sequence, we define how these insults shape cerebellar assembly during rapid maturation. Comparative analysis with human tissue confirmed that these insults recapitulate key features of the human preterm cerebellum, establishing the translational validity of this model for dissecting insult-specific outcomes. Behavioral and kinematic profiling revealed divergent motor and social phenotypes, which we traced to insult-specific cerebellar remodelling. Hypoxia compromised both granule cell maturation in the internal granule layer and the principal excitatory afferents to Purkinje cells, a circuit state that manifested as impaired motor execution and stereotyped, sensory-disengaged social investigation. Maternal immune activation, by contrast, expanded the granule cell progenitor layer and reduced Purkinje cell dendritic complexity, a phenotype that preserved social preference but reorganized the kinematic structure of social investigation. When hypoxia followed maternal immune activation, it acted on this primed substrate to produce a distinct state in which the features established by prior inflammation were compounded by granule cell proliferative arrest, progressive mitochondrial dysfunction, and aberrant, hyper-interactive social investigation. Together, these findings reframe prematurity-associated insults as cerebellar reprogramming events shaped by both the identity and sequence of insults, linking distinct mechanistic substrates to divergent neurodevelopmental outcomes.
abstract_zh: 摘要 早产幸存者常出现运动和社会认知障碍，提示小脑发育异常，但其潜在机制尚不清楚。一个关键挑战是早产涉及多种重叠的围产期损伤，它们共同作用于发育中的大脑，使得单独效应难以分离。本文在小鼠中模拟了两种主要的早产相关损伤：母体免疫激活（MIA）和新生儿缺氧（Hx）。通过控制时间和顺序，我们阐明了这些损伤如何在快速成熟期间塑造小脑组装。与人类组织的比较分析证实，这些损伤重现了人类早产小脑的关键特征，验证了该模型在解析损伤特异性结果方面的转化有效性。行为和运动学剖析显示出不同的运动和社会表型，我们将其追溯到损伤特异性的小脑重塑。缺氧损害了内层颗粒层的颗粒细胞成熟以及Purkinje细胞的主要兴奋性传入，导致运动执行受损和刻板、感官脱离的社会探究。相反，母体免疫激活扩张了颗粒细胞祖细胞层并降低了Purkinje细胞树突复杂度，保持了社会偏好但重组了社会探究的运动学结构。当缺氧跟随母体免疫激活时，它作用于这一已被预先激活的基质，产生了一个独特状态：先前炎症建立的特征被颗粒细胞增殖停滞、线粒体功能逐步下降以及异常、过度互动的社会探究所放大。综上所述，这些发现将早产相关损伤重新定义为由损伤身份和顺序共同塑造的小脑重编程事件，将不同的机制基础与多样的神经发育结果联系起来。
